methods.label: Nonzero multiples of a direction vector
methods.explanation: Multiplying a direction vector by a nonzero real number produces a vector that remains parallel to the line, so it is still a direction vector. The zero vector cannot serve as a direction vector.
methods.levelReason: The method uses the definition of a direction vector and elementary scalar multiplication of spatial vectors.
